discoveries.headline: Why an index exit matters for Strategy's bitcoin
discoveries.why: MSCI will drop Strategy, the biggest listed holder of bitcoin with 850,364 BTC, from its global indexes after 30 November under a new screen for 'non-operating' companies. CoinDesk's Omkar Godbole explains how that could squeeze the company's bitcoin-buying model, as its value has slipped from 3.4 times its bitcoin holdings at the peak to about 1.08 times. A clear lesson in how traditional markets and crypto are now tied together. Education, not advice.

discoveries.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin meet at APEC
discoveries.why: The White House has confirmed the first three-way meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, which runs 18 to 19 November. Al Jazeera's Shola Lawal sets out what's on the table, from nuclear arms control after the New START treaty lapsed in February to trade and energy. A useful primer before the headlines land today.

discoveries.headline: Australia's best nature photos of 2026
discoveries.why: From 2,129 entries by 501 photographers, WA's Matt Deakin was named Australian Geographic Nature Photographer of the Year for 'Ethereal Encounter'. Scroll on for Georgina Steytler's 'Insect Trails', Matt Cornish's threatened-species image 'Resilience: A Fight for Survival' and junior winner Aaryan Dhakal's 'Silent Grace'. A reminder of how wild and close to home this country is.

discoveries.headline: Five minutes of gentle presence
discoveries.why: Canadian teacher Sarah Blondin guides you back into your body with gentle movement, breath and stillness, in just 5 minutes 27 seconds. It has been played more than 110,000 times on Insight Timer, and it's free. Try it before you open your inbox.

discoveries.headline: Why do we ignore weather warnings?
discoveries.why: In the 400th episode of the APA's Speaking of Psychology, Kim Mills talks with psychologists Brett Gelino (UMass Lowell) and Gabrielle Wong-Parodi (Stanford) about how people actually decide what to do as a storm approaches. They cover why alerts lose their urgency, how neighbours sway decisions to leave, and what makes a warning land. Timely listening as Australia heads into bushfire and storm season.
discoveries.source: Speaking of Psychology · American Psychological Association
discoveries.meta_credit: American Psychological Association · Speaking of Psychology · Kim I. Mills

discoveries.headline: Cellist Charlotte Miles wins Young Performers
discoveries.why: Melbourne cellist Charlotte Miles, 23, has won the 2026 ABC Young Performers Awards after playing Elgar's Cello Concerto with the Sydney Symphony Orchestra in the Sydney Opera House. She takes home $40,000 and a solo album on ABC Classic, and, in her words, 'I felt really calm out there.' Violinist Beatrice Colombis came second and 14-year-old pianist Dillon Chan third: three young talents to follow.
discoveries.meta_credit: The Violin Channel · ABC Young Performers Awards

discoveries.headline: A cooling cucumber drink for pitta season
discoveries.why: As Sydney warms up, Ayurveda turns to cooling foods for pitta. Michele Schulz of The Ayurvedic Institute, building on a Vasant Lad recipe, blends cucumber, mint, milk and a little coconut butter and maple syrup into a simple summer drink. A small, refreshing ritual for hot afternoons. General information, not medical advice.

discoveries.headline: Fifteen minutes to let stress go
discoveries.why: Sarah Beth, who has taught yoga for more than 15 years, leads a gentle, beginner-friendly flow from child's pose and thread-the-needle through cat-cow, half pigeon and happy baby to a final rest. She cues slow ujjayi and belly breathing throughout and closes on santosha, contentment. Free to follow along on video.

discoveries.headline: Lifting protects muscle while losing weight
discoveries.why: In UWA's T-REx study, published in Nature Medicine, 120 people aged 50 to 70 taking the weight-loss drug tirzepatide all lost about 22 kg over 40 weeks. Those who also did three resistance sessions a week lost 25% less lean tissue and gained 10% in strength, while the others lost 10%. As Professor Danny Green puts it, the goal is health and function, not just a lower number on the scales.
